content:
The test image shows a tomato stem near the soil line with:
- White/bleached area with white cottony mycelium on the stem
- Small dark rounded bodies (sclerotia) visible embedded in the white growth
- Upper plant appears wilted/dead
- Damage at the soil line level

This strongly suggests either Southern_Blight (small mustard-seed sclerotia + white mycelium at stem base) or Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (larger rice-grain sclerotia + white mycelium). Let me use my reference image on Southern_Blight to confirm.

The reference image shows an internal stem cross-section with vascular browning, not matching the test image. 

The test image features are clear:
- **White cottony mycelium** coating the stem at soil line
- **Small dark spherical sclerotia** (mustard-seed sized) embedded in the white growth
- Plant collapse/wilt above
- Infection right at/near soil line

This matches **Southern_Blight** (Sclerotium rolfsii) — "white cottony mycelium at stem base" with "spherical sclerotia ranging from light tan to dark reddish-brown to black, approximately the size of mustard seeds." The sclerotia visible are small and multiple, unlike Sclerotinia's larger rice-grain-sized sclerotia.

This matches Southern Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii) signature symptoms. Distinguished from Sclerotinia Timber Rot by the smaller, mustard-seed-sized sclerotia rather than the larger rice-grain-sized sclerotia of Sclerotinia."}
